reason: The cited evidence supports that laser cladding offers low dilution, rapid cooling, and metallurgical bonding (E2), and that HEAs have high corrosion resistance and excellent mechanical properties (E3). E2 and E3 also support laser cladding as a repair method for wear resistance. E1 supports surface cladding for enhancing wear/corrosion resistance. However, no cited evidence directly supports the key premise that the HEA coating reduces hot cracking risk compared to fusion welding, nor the specific synergistic mechanisms (cocktail, lattice distortion, sluggish diffusion) claimed.
premises: Laser cladding provides low dilution, rapid cooling, and metallurgical bonding.
HEAs possess unique structures that yield high corrosion resistance and excellent mechanical properties.
Laser cladding is an effective method for repairing damaged areas and enhancing surface wear resistance.
Surface cladding with wear- and corrosion-resistant alloys can enhance surface properties of steel.
